deviation_from_street.reason: Our end-2029 value ($34.66) is 21% below the $43.83 mean of 12 price targets, and on a like-for-like horizon the gap is wider: discounted at 12% it is about $24.67 today. The difference is weights, dilution and probability: the Street's mean needs bull-like weights (20/55/25 with the bull at a $3.5B peak and 75% gives $46.38), while we fund a Phase 3 and three autoimmune programs through 2029 with $600M of equity at $32 in the base and hold the weighted probability of XmAb819 approval at 38.5%, close to October's, because no new efficacy data have come out since ESMO.

thesis: Q3 confirmed the funding story, not the drug story. Revenue of $116.5M was $77.4M of Alexion settlement consideration and a $25.0M Astellas Phase 3 milestone; royalties excluding the settlement were about $10M. With $66.9M from selling two-thirds of the Zenas stake, cash and debt securities held at $555.7M, the year-end guide rose to $480-500M and the runway moved into 2029. XmAb819 is unchanged since ESMO: a 45.5% confirmed ORR in 11 patients at the 400 µg/kg RP3D, FDA talks and fuller data in 1H27, a Phase 3 against tivozanib by YE2027. On end-2029 values of $1.70 / $34.61 / $84.25 at 30/50/20 the weighted value is $34.66, 1.4% a year from $33.26: Watch with a negative bias, close to the Avoid line. The cases split on the 1H27 cohort update, and until it comes the price already pays for most of the base: a 45% chance of approval at $2B of peak sales, a 3.35x NPV-to-peak multiple and a $600M raise. Own at about $22.80.
consensus_view: Fourteen analysts (S&P Global, November 19) rate the stock Buy; the mean of 12 price targets is $43.83 ($26-$70), up from $40.25 at the October call; J.P. Morgan raised its target to $37 from $21 at Neutral after renal oncologist checks, and RBC ($43), Wedbush ($45), Canaccord ($40) and Leerink ($41) kept Buy after Q3. Consensus revenue is $198.65M for FY2026 and $115.79M for FY2027, with non-GAAP EPS of -$2.30 and -$3.79. The stock rose 14% on November 4 ahead of the after-close Q3 report and to $39.97 after the ACR data, then gave most of it back to $33.26 by November 20.
variant_view: The Street's $43.83 mean of 12 price targets, a 12-month price, sits above our end-2029 value of $34.66 (about $24.67 today at 12%). We do not think the price assumes the October data are confirmed: our base, a 25-45% confirmed rate, is worth $34.61 at end-2029, just above $33.26. The disagreement is with the Street's weights. Its mean needs the bull to be about as likely as the base (20/55/25 with the bull at a $3.5B peak and 75% gives $46.38), while five responses in 11 patients and the usual fade of later solid-tumor T-cell engager cohorts put us at 30/50/20, with only a 0.20 chance the full cohort holds 45%. Checkable (claim x819-orr-25-1h27, 0.65 the other way): if the 1H27 update shows a confirmed ORR below 25%, or no update covering 20 or more patients by July 31, 2027, we expect XNCR below $20 by the end of 2027.

notes: The October call was a backfill whose values were today-values from an rNPV discounted at 12%; this update states end-2029 values, undiscounted, as the IONS and NBIS updates do. Discounted at 12% for three years, $34.66 is about $24.67 today, 29% below October's $34.71: the base now pays for a Phase 3 and the autoimmune programs through 2029, sells $600M of equity at $32 and funds OMERS shortfalls, deducts the OMERS liability left at end-2029, and the weights moved to 30/50/20 from 25/50/25.

XmAb819 at end-2029 is peak sales x probability of approval x October's NPV-to-peak multiple rolled forward three years at 12% (2.0x to 2.8x bear; 2.5x to 3.5x base and bull). Probabilities stay near October's: weighted 38.5% at end-2029 (0.30 x 10% + 0.50 x 45% + 0.20 x 65%) against 36% today in October, because no new efficacy data came out. Peaks are October's ($800M / $2.0B / $3.0B). The first draft raised the bull to $3.5B at 70% and the base to 50%, which the review rejected.

Weights follow the 1H27 cohort update: bear if the confirmed ORR settles below about 25% or tolerability fails (30%), base for about 25-45% (50%), bull at 45% or more with an accelerated path (20%). Five confirmed responses in 11 patients have a 95% interval of roughly 17% to 77%, and later cohorts in solid-tumor T-cell engagers usually come in below early ones, so the claims put 0.65 on at least 25% and 0.20 on at least 45%. Some of the 35% chance of missing 25% is a delayed or thin update, not a failed drug, which is why the bear weight is 30%.

Net cash starts at the midpoint of the YE2026 guide ($490M of cash, cash equivalents and marketable debt securities). The remaining Zenas stake ($27.0M at September 30) is left out in case the guide already counts a Q4 sale; adding it is worth $0.27 a share. Burn each year is operating expenses less stock comp and D&A ($35-45M), less cash revenue (revenue less $24M a year of ex-U.S. Ultomiris royalties paid straight to OMERS, $12M in 2029), less net interest, less the final $52.5M Alexion installment in 2027, plus $5M of capex, plus $11M a year in 2027-2028 of shortfall funding: under the settlement Xencor funds shortfalls in the up to $35M a year OMERS is owed through 2028, and ex-U.S. Ultomiris royalties ran about $6.1M a quarter in Q3. The 10-Q does not give the shortfall terms; $5.0M of restricted cash is held against them. Without the charge the value is $34.89. Leases ($55M at end-2029) are deducted, and so is what is left of the OMERS liability at end-2029, about $44M ($95.1M accreting at its 17.0% effective rate, less about $35M a year paid in 2027-2028 and $12M in 2029), as October deducted the whole liability; it costs $0.45 a share. Royalties and milestones ($150M / $200M / $280M), other pipeline ($50M / $150M / $350M) and overhead (-$250M / -$300M / -$250M) stay at October's today-values and are not rolled forward, because their 2027-2029 receipts and costs are already in the burn.

FY2027 base revenue is $90M, about $40M of royalties (ex-U.S. Ultomiris about $24M, Monjuvi about $16M) and about $50M of milestones (for example an obexelimab approval under the Zenas agreements, or xaluritamig and ASP2138 events), below the $115.79M consensus. The $52.5M Alexion installment is cash in 2027 but was revenue in 2026, so it is added separately and is not in revenue.

Shares start at 78.353M, the Q3 diluted weighted average, which counts in-the-money options because Q3 was profitable (74.76M issued at September 30 and 75.04M at October 30; Q3 basic weighted shares of 76.215M suggest some pre-funded warrants from September 2024 remain unexercised after 1.388M were exercised in Q1). Shares grow 2% a year from stock compensation ($28.2M in nine months 2026). The base raise at $32 sits near the base path's 2027-2028 prices less an offering discount.

Sensitivities (all printed by the build script): weights 25/50/25 $38.79 (5.3%), 35/45/20 $33.02 (-0.2%), 40/45/15 $28.89 (-4.6%), 20/55/25 $40.44 (6.7%); October's XmAb819 inputs rolled forward $29.45 (-4.0%); base probability 35% $31.23, 60% $39.82; base peak $1.5B $30.80, $2.5B $38.53; base multiple 3.0x $32.45; all multiples 3.0x (2.5x bear) $30.41 (-2.9%); base raise at $22 $33.33, at $40 $35.32; bull $3.5B at 75% $39.42, and with 20/55/25 $46.38 (11.7%); XmAb942 $300M in base $35.15, zero $33.68; Zenas stake added $34.94. The base NPV-to-peak multiple that returns $33.26 is 3.35x. The bull carries $16.85 of the $34.66.
Base rates: revenue CAGR is not a meaningful reference class for a clinical-stage biotech whose 2027-2029 revenue is royalties and milestones, so no base_rate block is set.

The November 23 close of $35.17 (StockAnalysis) was not yet in data/prices/XNCR.csv when the call was written; the call uses the November 20 close of $33.26, at which the rule gives Watch (1.4% a year). At $35.17 the weighted value is -0.5% a year, past the Avoid line; if the price is still above about $34.70 at the January review the call moves to Avoid.

Review round 1 (agent:reviewing-research, grade C): the first draft (25/50/25, fair value $44.73, 10.4% a year) raised XmAb819 inputs without new efficacy data (base 40% to 50%; bull $3.0B x 45% x 2.5x to $3.5B x 70% x 3.0x) and did not show the bull and bear changes; claims at 0.45-0.50 contradicted 75% weight on base plus bull; the base raise at $40 sat above its own price path; recurring Q3 revenue was misstated as about $12M; the OMERS liability was called non-recourse, which the 10-Q does not say, and the shortfall funding was ignored; the variant view compared end-2029 values with 12-month targets; the first kill criterion did not fire on a delayed or thin update. All fixed as described in review.response.

Review round 2 (agent:reviewing-research, grade C): the second draft ($37.32, 3.9% a year) had moved royalties, other pipeline and overhead above October's values without saying so (worth $2.02 a share), dropped the OMERS liability left at end-2029, priced the bull's 2027 raise at $55 against a $46 path, kept stale figures in two catalysts, the pre-mortem and change_my_mind, and kept a variant view its own base contradicted. All fixed as described in review.response; fair value is now $34.66.

low_score_reasons: evidence: Royalties (150/200/280 to 200/300/400), other pipeline (50/150/350 to 50/250/500) and bear overhead (-250 to -150) changed from October with no stated basis; the royalty line appears rolled forward at 12% even though its 2027-2029 receipts are already in the burn, the residual OMERS liability (about $44M at end-2029 on 17% accretion and $35/$35/$12M of payments) is no longer deducted although October deducted it, and the Amgen $225M milestone and TIVO-3 18% ORR have no saved source.

valuation: The report says 'The only uplift is October's NPV-to-peak multiples rolled forward', but the undisclosed royalty, other-pipeline and overhead changes add $2.02 a share; at October's values for those three lines the model gives $35.39 (2.1% a year), and the change table omits all three rows.

variant_view: The claim that the market is 'paying for the October dataset as if it were already confirmed' is contradicted by the call's own base: a 25-45% ORR outcome (not confirmation) is worth $37.00 at 3.5x, above $33.26, and the price needs only 3.08x; the checkable test uses a 35% threshold that sits inside the call's own base band and is not a recorded claim.

calibration: A weighted 38.5% chance of approval for a Phase 1 asset with 5 responses in 11 patients is high for oncology and is not defended against any reference class; base plus bull (70%) assume a Phase 3 around YE2027 while the Phase 3 claim is 0.45, and the scenarios imply about a 0.70 chance of selling at least $200M of stock in 2027 against the 0.60 claim.
review.counter_case: On its own numbers this is an Avoid at the price the stock already trades at. Put the royalty, other-pipeline and overhead lines back at October's values, which the report never says it changed, and the value is $35.39, 0.2% a year from the $35.17 November 23 close; set the bear weight to the 0.35 the call itself gives to missing 25% (35/45/20) and it is $33.75, -1.4% a year. All of this still assumes a 38.5% chance of approval for a drug whose evidence is five responses in eleven patients, and the base and bull cases both need a Phase 3 around YE2027 that the call gives only a 0.45 chance. The 'negative bias' is the call admitting it is one honest adjustment away from Avoid.
review.response: Accepted on every defect; fair value cut again, from $37.32 (3.9% a year) to $34.66 (1.4%). Royalties, other pipeline and overhead go back to October's today-values ($150M/$200M/$280M, $50M/$150M/$350M, -$250M/-$300M/-$250M) and are not rolled forward, because their 2027-2029 receipts and costs are in the burn; the report's change table now shows them. The OMERS liability left at end-2029 (about $44M) is deducted, -$0.45 a share. The bull raises $400M at $45 in 2027 and $400M at $55 in 2028. Catalyst values, the pre-mortem price, change_my_mind ($46.38 at 20/55/25 with the bull at $3.5B and 75%), the projection's FY2027 revenue reason, the FY2027 EPS gap (pre-raise base -$3.75 against the Street's -$3.79), the unsourced Amgen $225M, the FDA wording and the 12-target count are fixed. The equity-raise claim moves to 0.70 to match the scenarios, and the base basis says a Phase 3 start up to mid-2028 is still the base. The variant view is restated as a disagreement with the Street's weights, tested by claim x819-orr-25-1h27. On the counter-case: at 35/45/20 the revised model gives $33.02, -0.2% a year from $33.26, and at the $35.17 close the 30/50/20 value is -0.5% a year, so the call sits on the Avoid line. We keep Watch at the $33.26 reference price, where the rule gives 1.4% a year, because some of the 35% chance of missing 25% is a delayed or thin update rather than a failed drug, and a 25-35% confirmed rate against tivozanib's 18% in TIVO-3 is still a registrable drug. We record that a price still above about $34.70 at the January 9 review moves the call to Avoid. We do not cut the 38.5% weighted approval probability further: it is held to October's 36% plus three years of resolution, and the review gives no reference class that would set a different number.
